seo.title: Holiday Search Features: What Local Shops Can Do
seo.meta_description: Holiday search features let shoppers find local in-stock decor with Lens and book hotels, dinners and shows in AI Mode. What Orange County businesses should do.

h1: Holiday Search Features: How Lens and AI Mode Send Shoppers to Local Businesses
answer: Google's holiday search features, shared on November 16, 2026, include Lens showing shoppable links and local in-stock options for decor seen in photos, AI Mode comparing and booking hotels, finding restaurant tables by party size and time, and tracking event tickets. Anaheim and Orange County shops, restaurants, hotels and venues should make their stock, availability and booking details easy for Google to read.
key_takeaways: Lens shows local in-stock options for items in a photo.
AI Mode compares hotels and can complete some bookings.
AI Mode finds restaurant tables by party size and time.
Search can track ticket drops for sold-out shows.

sections.heading: What Google shared
sections.body_html: On November 16, 2026, Google shared four ways Search can help with holiday plans: Search Live for real-time help, Lens for recreating decor, AI Mode for booking getaways and dinners, and AI Mode for finding event tickets.

sections.heading: Lens finds local in-stock items
sections.body_html: Google's example: someone photographs a festive tablescape at a local restaurant or online and asks Lens to help find the pieces. Google says Search breaks the scene into items and shows shoppable links and local in-stock options.

sections.heading: AI Mode books hotels
sections.body_html: Google says people can describe a destination, dates and preferences in AI Mode to compare stays by amenities, reviews and photos, then click out to book with travel partners, or in some cases complete the reservation in AI Mode with Google Pay.

sections.heading: AI Mode finds restaurant tables
sections.body_html: People can tell AI Mode what they're craving, plus party size and time, and Google says Search pulls together available tables matching the criteria so they can complete the booking.

sections.heading: AI Mode tracks tickets
sections.body_html: For events, Google says AI Mode can compare tickets across partners and, if a show is sold out or tickets aren't on sale yet, track ticket drops and price changes and send a notification.

sections.heading: Search Live in the kitchen
sections.body_html: Google also highlights Search Live, where people point their camera at a cooking problem and ask for help by voice. It's a reminder that more searches now start with a camera rather than typed words.

sections.heading: What this means for retailers
sections.body_html: Local in-stock options only appear for retailers whose store inventory Google can see. Home decor, gift and party stores in Orange County can use free local listings and accurate product data so their items show up when shoppers photograph something they want.

sections.heading: What this means for restaurants
sections.body_html: For AI Mode to find your available tables, your reservation system needs to work with Google's booking partners and your Business Profile needs a working reservation link. Check both before the busiest weeks.

sections.heading: What this means for hotels
sections.body_html: Hotels near Anaheim's Resort District and the coast compete on amenities, reviews and photos in these comparisons. Keep amenity lists, room photos and rates accurate across your website and the partners you use.

sections.heading: What this means for venues
sections.body_html: Venues and event organizers should make ticket pages clear, with dates, prices and on-sale times, so ticket-tracking features can pick up updates when tickets are released.

sections.heading: A holiday checklist
sections.body_html:
1. Turn on free local listings if you sell in a store.
  2. Check your reservation link works with Google.
  3. Update amenities, photos and rates for hotels.
  4. Publish clear ticket and on-sale details.
  5. Update special holiday hours.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a home decor shop in Brea. A shopper photographs a holiday table setting at a restaurant and asks Lens where to buy similar pieces. Because the shop has added its in-store stock to Google, its candle holders and table runners appear among the local in-stock options, and the shopper visits that afternoon.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they need special software to appear in Lens results. Retailers need product and store inventory data on Google, usually through Merchant Center. Another common question is whether restaurants must use a particular booking system. Check that your reservation provider works with Google's booking features. Owners also ask whether small hotels can compete with chains in AI Mode comparisons. Yes, on reviews, photos and specific amenities guests care about.

sections.heading: Photograph your products well
sections.body_html: Lens matches what shoppers photograph to products it knows. Clear photos of your items from the angles people see them in real life, with accurate names and descriptions, make it more likely Google connects a shopper's photo to your stock.

sections.heading: Keep availability current
sections.body_html: During the holidays, stock and availability change daily. Retailers should update inventory often, restaurants should keep reservation availability current, and hotels should make sure rates and room types match across partners, so AI features don't send customers to something unavailable.

sections.heading: Tell customers what you offer
sections.body_html: Holiday shoppers search for gifts, decor, dining and events with specific needs. A short page on your website listing holiday hours, gift ideas, private dining or group bookings gives Google and AI features more to work with.

sections.heading: Getting store inventory onto Google
sections.body_html: For retailers, the practical route to appearing in local in-stock results is Google Merchant Center. Set up a Merchant Center account, add your products, connect your Google Business Profile, and turn on free local listings with an inventory feed showing which products are in each store. Many point-of-sale systems can export inventory automatically. Start with your best-selling and most giftable products, keep stock levels updated daily during the holidays, and check Merchant Center for any issues that stop products from showing.

sections.heading: Restaurants: make holiday bookings easy
sections.body_html: Holiday diners often book for larger groups and special occasions. Make it clear online how far ahead reservations open, the largest party size you take online, whether you offer private dining or set menus, and any deposits or cancellation rules. Keep your reservation system's availability current, and add holiday hours to your Business Profile early. When AI Mode looks for tables that match a party size and time, accurate availability is what puts your restaurant in front of the guest.

sections.heading: Hotels and venues near Anaheim
sections.body_html: Hotels near the Anaheim Resort District and venues across Orange County see some of their busiest weeks around the holidays. Keep amenity lists specific, such as parking, shuttles, family rooms or fireplaces, and make sure rates and room types match across your website and booking partners. Venues should publish event dates, ticket prices and on-sale times clearly, so search features can pick up changes as soon as they happen.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google's holiday search features find local in-stock items from photos and book hotels, tables and tickets in AI Mode. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should make stock, availability and booking details easy for Google to read before the holiday rush.

faqs.q: Can Google Lens show local in-stock items?
faqs.a: Yes. Google says Lens shows shoppable links and local in-stock options for items in a photo.
Google says people can compare stays and, in some cases, complete the reservation in AI Mode.

faqs.q: Can AI Mode find restaurant tables?
faqs.a: Yes, by craving, party size and time, according to Google.
Google says it can track ticket drops and price changes and send notifications.

faqs.q: How do retailers appear in Lens local results?
faqs.a: With product and store inventory data on Google.
